extracted.intended_audience: trademark and design practitioners, IP attorneys, patent court judges, and legal scholars (Korean IP context)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes legal standards and evaluative criteria used by the Korean Patent Court for deciding trademark and design registration, invalidation, cancellation, and scope-of-rights disputes. Covers distinctiveness, similarity, prior use, unfair purpose/use, non-use cancellation, geographical names, celebrity names, flag similarity, and design creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive mark / Lack of distinctiveness (Article 6(1)3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark that would be recognized by traders or consumers as indicating a quality or effect of the designated goods (e.g., meaning 'a toothbrush of which bristles are planted in 360' or 'a toothbrush with bristles can rotate 360') is a trademark consisting solely of marks indicating quality and effect in a common manner of use, isn't itself distinctive but is just a descriptive mark, and therefore is not eligible for registration pursuant to Article 6(1)3 of the Trademark Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess what the public (general traders or consumers) would understand the mark to mean when used with the designated goods. If the ordinary understanding of the mark only describes a characteristic, quality or effect of the goods, the mark is descriptive and unregistrable. (Example: literal descriptions of product features.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous geographical name
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical name used by a lot of people in a specified region can be seen as a conspicuous geographical name even if the name is not conspicuously known nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider evidence of local usage and recognition: presence as river/administrative zone/market/road/station/restaurant names, number of commercial uses (e.g., many bistros using the name), long-standing association with a local product (e.g., 'Sincheon tteokbokki' known regionally). Regional prominence (e.g., in Daegu) suffices to find the name conspicuous for purposes of refusal or limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity to national flag (Article 7(1)1-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark that is similar to the flag of a nation (e.g., same color arrangement and similar horizontal/vertical proportions) should be rejected under Article 7(1)1-2 of the Trademark Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess overall visual similarity, color order, proportions (e.g., 4:3), and whether added small elements (e.g., a small hot-air balloon) are sufficiently distinctive relative to the whole. Small additions that occupy a small area and preserve the dominant arrangement do not avoid similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark containing the name/title/acronym of a celebrity (Article 7(1)6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any trademark containing the name, title, trade name, portrait, signature, seal, literary name, stage name, pen name of a prominent person, or his/her abbreviated title shall not be registered as a trademark (Article 7(1)6). The provision's purpose is to protect moral rights of another person; it does not primarily seek to prevent confusion of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a person is 'prominent' should be judged considering period, manner, type and frequency of use, scope of trading and reality of trading of goods using the name, and whether the name becomes widely recognized in ordinary life or the relevant trading society. Registration may be possible with the celebrity's approval (proviso). Example: evaluate popularity, awards, media presence (e.g., T-ara's career and recognition as of application date). Also consider whether a mark actually includes the celebrity's exact name or is merely similar or an established prior emblem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity to a pre-registered trademark (likelihood of confusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A challenged trademark may be found similar to a pre-registered trademark if consumers are likely to misunderstand or confuse the origin of goods or services; similarity analysis considers meanings associated with the marks, business particulars, scope of trading, and consumer perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare semantic associations of the marks (e.g., one means 'next in line', the other means 'beauty/manliness'), the plaintiff's corporate image and long-term use, consumers' recognition in the trading society, and real-world evidence of confusion or lack thereof. The absence of observed consumer confusion and distinct meanings can support a finding of non-similarity (example: Kakao/Daum case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior/pre-used trademark widely known (ground for invalidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-used trademark or service mark that was widely known among domestic consumers or traders as indicating goods/services of the prior user at the time a registered trademark was determined may invalidate the later registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate extent of recognition with objective evidence: release date and rapid growth (installations/users), market share, number of users, news coverage and awards, and whether the mark functions as a distinctive indication beyond being merely a product name. Also assess economic relevance between goods/services (e.g., commercialization of game characters onto household goods, mobile brands commercializing characters across many item types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of relevance between designated goods and prior goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing conflict between a registered trademark and a pre-used mark, determine the degree to which the registered goods are relevant to the goods/services associated with the pre-used mark in economic respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider actual commercialization (character goods, spin-off products), precedence of similar marketing (e.g., other portals commercializing characters on toothpaste/toothbrush), whether designated goods are easily developed as character goods, and market practices showing brands extend characters across product categories. Close economic relevance supports likelihood of confusion/invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark applied with unfair purpose (Article 7(1)12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark that is the same with or similar to a pre-used or pre-registered mark recognized as indicating goods of a certain person may fall under Article 7(1)12 if applied for with unjust purpose (unfair intent). If there was no unjust purpose at the time of application, the mark does not fall under Article 7(1)12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess facts for unfair purpose: whether the applicant intended to damage intangible value (business reputation/customer drawing power), interfere with right holder's operations, take unfair benefit from the pre-existing mark, or otherwise acted with unfair intent. Consider prior independent use, lack of imitation in color/design, differences in goods/services, and common-word status (example: 'FLUKE' clothing vs. Fluke electronics). Existence of legitimate business use/licensing weighs against finding unfair purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair use of trademarks (Article 73(1)2) — transformed/continued use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a registered trademark that is transformed after registration to look more similar to a subject trademark, making consumer confusion more likely, falls under unfair use per Article 73(1)2. Likewise, if an actually used trademark (even if used before registration) continues to be used in a way that increases likelihood of confusion with another subject trademark, that continued use also falls under unfair use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish permissible minor transformations from material transformations that damage 'sameness'. The fact that the actually used mark predates registration does not preclude unfair-use cancellation if the use creates greater confusion than the registered form would have. Examine timing of transformations, extent of change, and resulting consumer confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation for non-use (Article 73(1)3) and 'interested person' standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration can be cancelled if the trademark holder, exclusive licensee or non-exclusive licensee, without proper reason, has not used the registered trademark domestically for more than three years prior to the cancellation claim (Article 73(1)3). An 'interested person' entitled to file such a claim means those directly and practically interested in extinction of the Registered Trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess standing by whether the claimant would be damaged or its legal status affected by the Registered Trademark (likelihood of future contestation, infringement suits, or registration rejections). 'Use' includes use by licensees under trademark license contracts. Evaluate evidence of domestic use; licensing and royalty receipts alone do not negate an assessment of non-use if use is absent, but licensing activity can indicate intention to use and weigh against a finding of non-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of confirmation in scope-of-rights actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registered service mark holder requests a decision confirming that a subject service mark belongs to the scope of rights, benefit of confirmation is judged at time of decision; if the respondent implemented the subject mark prior to decision and sameness is unacknowledged, the confirmation only applies to the specific subject mark as applied and may lack practical effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, benefit of confirmation requires that the subject mark be implemented as of the decision; exceptionally, benefit may be acknowledged if the respondent implemented before decision but is likely to implement in the future. Cite prior precedent when assessing benefit (Supreme Court decisions referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design creativity / aesthetic value for design invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a registered design imitates or transforms a prior design, it may be invalidated if the Registered Design lacks creativity and is merely a commercial/functional transformation whose aesthetic value is not recognized, or if it is only a change/composition/commonplace conversion in the design field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the dominant characteristic(s) attracting viewer attention (e.g., allocation/shape of components on a printed circuit board). Differences that are merely common color choices, simple commercial slants/angles, or commonplace reallocations are insufficient to establish creative individuality. Compare registered design and prior designs holistically to determine whether creative contribution exists beyond routine commercial modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parts of a composite mark / essential elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Registered Trademark is a composite mark made up of multiple symbols/characters/shapes and those elements are all essential, use of only a part of the composite mark cannot be acknowledged as use of the Registered Trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which components are essential to the whole mark. Transformed use is allowed only to the extent it does not damage the 'sameness' of the trademark; deletion of an essential element constitutes material transformation and is not equivalent to use of the full registered mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use as an indication of source — evidentiary threshold for consumer postings/transliterations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions found in consumer postings or transliterations (e.g., Korean transliteration of an English mark) do not automatically count as use as an indication of source; evidence must show the term is used in trade as indicating the source of goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the context and the probative value of examples: forum postings by consumers that do not clearly identify products do not suffice. Confirm that the mark was actually used commercially as a trademark (attached to goods, used in advertising/sales) rather than being merely descriptive or a consumer reference.
